transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?

My mind keeps swinging between being full of plans and then feeling so foggy that I can’t focus long enough to finish anything. It has been really disruptive, and I'm just having a hard time managing it lately.
Have you had periods lasting at least 4 days where you felt unusually energized or irritable, needed much less sleep, and were more talkative or impulsive than usual?

Yes, definitely—I have weeks-long stretches where I feel incredibly energized and stay up late working on tons of new projects, but I also get so irritable that I snap at my husband over tiny things. During those times, I talk in a nonstop stream that he can't even get a word into because my mind is just racing with ideas.
During those high-energy periods, have you ever had to be hospitalized, had major problems at work or in relationships, or done things that were clearly dangerous or out of character?

I’ve never been hospitalized, but these swings have caused major problems in my work and relationships. I’ve missed crucial grant deadlines, backed out of consulting work at the last minute, and had tense arguments with my husband about my unpredictable productivity. I've even let my friendships and community art group slide to the point where people don't feel they can rely on me anymore.

During those high-energy periods, did you ever feel so unusually confident or powerful that you took major risks, spent a lot of money, or made decisions that others said were clearly out of character?

During those high phases, I felt so confident that I'd tell people I was going to completely revolutionize art therapy in the city, talking like I'd already built this massive, successful practice. I didn't spend a lot of money or take physical risks, but I made highly unrealistic commitments overnight—like suddenly emailing a dozen organizations about huge collaborations—which others definitely saw as out of character and unsustainable.

Have you ever had a period of at least 1 week where these high-energy symptoms were so severe that they caused very serious problems, or required hospitalization, or were there times when you felt depressed for at least 2 weeks as well?

I’ve never been hospitalized, but these high-energy phases and the crashes afterward have been happening for about four months and have caused serious disruptions, like missing key deadlines and losing people's trust. As for the low, foggy, depressed-feeling stretches, those have been hanging around most days for the last three months.
Have you ever had a period of at least 1 week where you felt unusually energized or irritable with much less need for sleep and racing thoughts, even if you were not hospitalized?

Yes, absolutely. Over the last four months, I've had phases lasting for weeks where I feel incredibly energized, stay up late working on projects, and have thoughts racing like there are too many tabs open in my head. I also get extremely irritable and snap at my husband, and while I haven't been hospitalized, these periods have completely disrupted my life.
Have you ever had a period of at least 2 weeks where you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day, with loss of interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

Yes, for about the last three months, I've been in a low, foggy stretch where I've lost interest in almost everything I normally love doing. Things like my book club, sketching, and leading my community art group now feel like a massive chore, so I just end up scrolling on my phone instead of engaging.

Have you ever had a period of at least 1 week where you felt unusually energized or irritable with much less need for sleep, racing thoughts, and increased activity, even if you did not need hospitalization?

Yes, absolutely. Ever since I left my steady job about four months ago, I've had weeks-long stretches where my thoughts race constantly like open tabs in my head and I stay up late working on projects with endless physical energy. During those weeks, I swing between feeling incredibly upbeat and snapping irritably at my husband over the tiniest things.

During your high-energy periods, do the symptoms last at least 4 days and feel clearly different from your usual self, but not so severe that you need hospitalization or completely lose touch with reality?

Yes, those high-energy phases last for weeks at a time and are completely different from my normal self, which my husband and friends definitely notice. While they cause real disruption to my work and relationships, they've never been severe enough to require hospitalization, and I've never lost touch with reality.

opening_question.question: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview supports a bipolar disorder diagnosis with clear recurrent hypomanic/manic-spectrum episodes lasting weeks, featuring markedly increased energy, decreased need for sleep, racing thoughts, pressured nonstop speech, irritability, grandiose/unrealistic goal-directed activity, and major functional disruption. The patient also reports a concurrent depressive period lasting about 3 months with loss of interest and low motivation. No psychosis or hospitalization was reported. The overall picture is most consistent with bipolar affective disorder (ICD-10 F31).
